To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have computed the NLO forward jet vertex for the first time and have shown that it is finite.
the forward jet vertex at NLO has been calculated in the BFKL formalism, making use of the eective action proposed recently by Lipatov.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the vertex for the coupling of a hard pompon to a forward jet at NLO in the BFKL formalism.
the study of the NLO vertex for a forward rapidity gap plus a jet at high energies.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the BFKL approach to high-energy scattering is still a viable and promising option to understand the dynamics at high energies, and that the next-to-leading order calculation of the forward-jet vertex is an important ingredient to this aim.

the BFKL approach, at least at NLO, is able to describe the main features of the rapidity gap structure in diffractive events, and it is a very promising tool for the description of the jet production in diffractive processes.
the BFKL approach is not yet mature enough to describe jet production in dijet events, and the main reason is that the NLO corrections are not under control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a fixed rapidity gap, we are able to compute the NLO jet vertex for a forward rapidity gap, in the BFKL formalism.
we are now able to compute, at NLO accuracy, the production of two jets in the diffractive channel.

, in a forthcoming paper, we shall present the first NLO calculations of the forward jet production in a diffractive environment, in which we shall include both the NLO nonforward gluon Green function and the NLO forward jet vertex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NLO vertex for the forward jet is not universal, but depends on the rapidity gap, i.e., it has a different form depending on whether the jet is emitted before or after the rapidity gap.
the vertex is not a simple product of the NLO forward gluon Green function with the LO vertex, as naively expected from the high energy eective action.
the high-energy eective action is a powerful tool for the study of jet production in the BFKL formalism at NLO.
